description.narrative: IFC is considering providing an up to US$40 million loan to Knight Therapeutics Inc. (Knight or the Company), a pan-American (ex-USA) specialty pharmaceutical company headquartered in Canada with significant operations in Latin America, to partially finance the acquisition of the rights to manufacture, market and sell Exelon® (rivastigmine) in Canada and Latin America (the Territory), as well as an exclusive license to use the intellectual property and the Exelon® trademark, from Novartis within the Territory (the Exelon Acquisition). Exelon® is indicated for the symptomatic treatment of mild to moderately severe dementia in people with Alzheimers disease and Parkinsons disease. Founded in 2014 in Montreal, Canada, Knight is pan-American (ex-USA) specialty pharmaceutical company that focused on acquiring or in-licensing and commercializing pharmaceutical products in Canada and Latin America. In 2019, Knight acquired a controlling stake in Grupo Biotoscana (GBT), a specialty pharmaceutical company with a presence across Latin America. In August 2020, Knight completed the 100% acquisition of GBT. With the GBT acquisition, Knight has expanded its operations in Latin America through a direct presence in 10 countries.

Project outcomes: The Project helps respond to the existing and growing need for effective pharmaceuticals to treat dementia. Both Alzheimer's and Parkinson's are a fast-growing burden of disease in Latin America due to the rapidly aging population. Exelon® acts to reduce symptoms by slowing down the degradation of acetylcholine. Knight plans to actively promote Exelon® to revive a brand that has good brand equity and is accepted for its superior quality and tolerance. The patch form of Exelon® has been shown to have less side effects and provides convenience for patients and their caregivers, which is particularly important given the challenges patients with dementia face taking medication.
Contribution to market creation: IFC anticipates that the Project will result in an increase in disease awareness, diagnosis and access to treatment in Brazil and other countries in Latin America through the improved promotion of the medication. Absent Knight's acquisition, access to Exelon® may have potentially been limited given the current under-investments in the product, and as a result knowledge of the effectiveness of the product and its market share could fall. The declining role of Exelon® would in turn lead to a further reduction in disease awareness, diagnosis, and access to treatment in the market. In particular, without Knight's acquisition, continued under-investment would cause a negative impact on the attractiveness of the market and would contribute to an under-developed market with less treatment options.
